what_was_done: The rewind half is closed: every state push carries --force-with-lease naming its base, a lost race needs a head that contains the base, and scenario 7 covers a rewind between the opening sync and the claim push (fact 16 rerun on git 2.34.1 and 2.50.1: a plain push after a rewind to an ancestor exits 0 and restores the commit, the lease push exits 1 with stale info and leaves the remote alone). The arrivals half is still open. T-PUSH has T-HISTORY judge the fetch made after a push that did not report success 'as at any sync', and T-HISTORY writes sync.remote_head 'here, when a fetched head has passed'. On a lost race the new head contains the base, so T-HISTORY passes and sync.remote_head moves to that head before anything has reached the mount. T-INCOMING checks only the files that differ between sync.remote_head and the fetched head. So when the sync repeats from its listing, or T-PUBLISH and T-MINT repeat from their opening sync, the commits between the base and that head are never checked. commands/sync.md step 3 can even end `synced` with no fetch, because the listed head equals sync.remote_head, and T-PUBLISH's accepted commit then brings those commits into the mount by a fast-forward, past T-INCOMING and T-HOLD. The same happens after an `accepted` judgement when others pushed on top. Fix: say in T-HISTORY that a fetch made to judge a push writes nothing. On a lost race sync.remote_head stays the push's base, and an accepted push sets it to the pushed commit, not to the remote's head. In commands/sync.md the step-3 shortcut also requires the mount's head to be sync.remote_head. Add to proof scenario 2 a record that fails its check, pushed by the winner, which the loser reports through T-INCOMING.

The head rule of table:team-checks is now the complete list, with T-DELIVERY in pr mode, T-REMOTE's ref rule and T-ORDER, and config/team.md, topics/team-use.md and the header of table:team-delivery-checks link to it. T-DELIVERY's merged_by and config/team.md's 'no survey fetches the state branch' are corrected. One file still keeps its own list. The last section of topics/team-sync.md ('One clone, or no remote') says: 'With team.enabled false nothing in this file runs, except that a push which finds the remote moved stops and says so (T-SOLO).' That contradicts the head rule as this correction extended it. T-REMOTE's choice of remote and refs (this file's 'No name' bullet) holds for every fetch and push. T-JOIN (its 'One shared repository' bullet) acts at vsdd init. T-ORDER (its 'Clocks' bullet) holds whatever the key says. Fix: replace that sentence with a link to the head rule of table:team-checks, and keep only 'With no remote there is nothing to sync and nothing changes.'
